observations: Two real zvec-grep services indexed and queried separate temporary workspaces while sharing one borrowed embedding model.
Closing service A before indexing and querying service B succeeded; closing either service left the caller-owned model usable.
The shared model dispose counter remained zero after both service closes and incremented only when the caller explicitly disposed the model.
Real prepared snapshots for Markdown, JSON, YAML configuration, and plaintext matched stock extraction fragments and vector composition.
The same snapshots were ingested through the real zvec-grep service and each format returned non-empty observable indexed context for a unique marker.
Reapplying prepared snapshots with a model whose embedding dimension differs from the published index is rejected with EMBEDDING_SCHEMA_CHANGE_REQUIRES_REBUILD.
A real prepared-batch rename deleted the old absolute file path, indexed the new path, and returned only the renamed file for the vector marker.
A subsequent real prepared-batch delete removed the renamed vector metadata; the same vector query returned zero items and filesDeleted=1.

Public codeIntel sync, file deletion, sync, and strict zvec search over an empty workspace returned status=empty with zvec outcome=empty, no issues, zero evidence, and a clean published retrieval view.
The fixed guard distinguishes sources: undefined (missing capture) from sources: [] (legitimate empty capture); the empty publication had no native file rows and no captured-source-unavailable error.
A public rename probe published after.txt, removed before.txt from native file rows and FTS hits, and returned anchored evidence at after.txt under a clean retrieval view.
Real retrieval contract evidence declares textKind=source and returns text equal to the complete UTF-8 source span captured by the canonical anchor, rather than a preview snippet.

The source anchor identity follows the effective captured range, including excerptRange for source-role context items whose displayed preview is shorter; the downstream verifier can therefore match the complete captured span while outline-role items remain descriptions.

Native zvec text ranges were reproduced with an oversized CRLF JavaScript fixture containing é/漢/emoji; web-tree-sitter and extractor ranges remained UTF-16 code-unit offsets, and the adapter converted them explicitly to UTF-8-byte anchors without content-based unit guessing.
Indexed source-role anchors are independently checked against the native excerpt content; lexical line matches and outline descriptions retain their distinct broader-content contracts.

A direct prepared zvec context query on the oversized fixture returned content equal to its excerptRange UTF-16 slice (including later value17), confirming the source-role equality check targets excerptRange rather than the broader entity range.
